sentences.text: Kiran vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited on 6 April, 2026

Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:8944
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 6 th Of April, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 4794 of 2025
 Kiran And Others
 Versus
 Oriental Insurance Company Limited And Others
 Appearance:
 Ms. Ayushi Thakur - Advocate for the appellants.
 Ms. Priti Keshwani, learned counsel for the responden
 Shri Pariksheetraj Singh Dodiya, learned counsel for 
 No.1.
 Order

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellants assailing the impugned award dated 3.3.2025 passed by Member 10th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 2522/2021, whereby an amount of Rs.12,09,000/-
along with interest has been awarded to the survivors of the deceased Harish, who passed away in road traffic accident which occurred on 28.4.2021 involving the offending vehicle motorcycle M.P.09 XB 8167.
2 .
Facts of the case are that on 28.4.2021 at about 9.00 Harsih was going towards Jagjeevanram Nagar by his motorcycle.

When he reached at Sheikh Hatim Tiraha Mandir at the same time the respondent No.2, the owner and driver of the vehicle came with the offending vehicle bearing NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8944 2 MA-4794-2025 registration No.MP 09 XB 8167 rashly and negligently and dashed the motorcycle of the deceased from backside.
Harish, the deceased suffered severe injuries and during treatment he died.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submits that the future prospect has not been awarded by the learned claims tribunal, which should have been awarded at 40% looking to the age of the deceased as he was 37 years of age at the time of the accident.

On the aforesaid alone ground,
a prayer for enhancement of the appropriate compensation has been sought.

4 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that learned Claims Tribunal has taken due care of all the parameters for assessing just and proper compensation, therefore, no interference is required by allowing this appeal, hence prays Kiran vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158452643/
1 for dismissal of the appeal.

entities.text: Kiran vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that looking to the number of survivors, 1/3rd be deducted.

5. Heard and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
The age of the deceased Harish on the date of accident was 37 is not in dispute.
Learned Claims Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding appropriate amount in the head of future prospects.
However looking to the age of the deceased 37 years, it should be 40% as per the directions given in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (2017) 16 SCC 680 (para 59.3 & 59.4).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant on this ground is accepted.

7. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation comes as under:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8944 3 MA-4794-2025 Rs.8,700/- pm + 40% FP Loss of Dependency: X 12 Months - 1/3rd PE X Multiplier of 15 =
Rs.14,61,600/-
 Consortium: Rs.1,32,000/- (40,000 x 3)
 Loss of Estate: Rs.16,500/-
 Funeral: Rs.16,500/-

Total Amount: Rs.16,26,600/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.12,09,000/-

Enhanced Amount: Rs.4,17,600/-
8 .
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.4,17,600/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.12,09,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellant(s) are entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.4,17,600/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
9 . The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate, which was fixed in the impugned award and the other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
10. Accordingly, the appeal stands partly allowed and disposed off in above terms.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
